answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may submit jobs or vote on outcomes. The protocol caps influence by locked stake, then slashes a stake when a randomly sampled, independently verifiable task exposes fraud. Splitting capital across a reef of identities does not multiply voting power; each new identity needs more locked funds and risks forfeiting them. The attacker pays an opportunity cost while honest agents can reclaim stake after the dispute window, whether their work tracks timber demand or a comet forecast.
